questions.q: What is a 'chunk' in the context of building a vector index over a catalog?
options: The unit of content you embed and later retrieve — for a catalog, one table's full profile including name, description, and columns
A single row of raw data from the table itself
A compiled binary file used to store the index
A random sample of unrelated tables grouped together
questions.explain: The chunk is what gets embedded and retrieved as one unit — the lesson uses one table's full profile as that unit.

questions.q: Why chunk by whole table rather than by individual column?
options: A question like 'which table has customer churn data?' needs table-level description and column context together in one retrieved unit, rather than forcing reassembly of fragments
Per-column chunking is always faster to embed
Column-level chunks contain more information than table-level chunks
Per-column chunking removes the need for any metadata
questions.explain: Splitting into per-column chunks would force retrieval to reassemble several fragments just to answer one question — more moving parts, more chances for an incomplete picture.

questions.q: What is the key rule about embedding models across chunks and questions?
options: Every chunk and every question must be embedded with the same model, or the resulting vectors aren't comparable
Different chunks can use different embedding models with no consequence
Only questions need to be embedded; chunks don't require embedding
The embedding model can change between indexing and retrieval without issue
questions.explain: Mixing embedding models makes the resulting vectors incomparable — consistency is the principle that matters more than which specific model is used.

questions.q: Besides the vector itself, what does a useful index entry need to store?
options: The original chunk text and metadata like the table name and workspace
Nothing else — the vector alone is sufficient for every use case
Only a randomly generated ID with no other information
The entire history of every query ever run against the index
questions.explain: Storing chunk text and metadata (table, workspace) is what lets a retrieved match be traced back to exactly where it came from.

questions.q: Why does storing table/workspace metadata alongside each vector matter for the next lesson's pipeline?
options: It lets the pipeline return not just an answer, but which table it came from, so the person asking can go verify it themselves
It has no effect on the pipeline's usefulness
It replaces the need for an embedding model entirely
It prevents the pipeline from ever retrieving the wrong table
questions.explain: This connects to the recurring 'check it before you trust it' habit from Lessons 45, 46, and 48 — traceability is what makes verification possible.
